clues.content: Who can accept residual security or continuity risk?

clues.title: Investigate
clues.content: Can temporary protections reduce exposure while testing finishes?

clues.title: Think deeper
clues.content: What verification and fallback will protect applicants if deployment fails?

presentationChoices.shortLabel: Install immediately because newer is safer
presentationChoices.fullDescription: Apply the update without testing or a recovery plan.
presentationChoices.feedback: Patching can be essential, but an untested production change can cause avoidable applicant harm.

presentationChoices.shortLabel: Assess urgency and authorize a tested plan
presentationChoices.fullDescription: Verify the threat, test critical paths, and choose controlled deployment or documented temporary mitigation.
presentationChoices.feedback: This makes the security and continuity tradeoff explicit and assigns decision and recovery ownership.

presentationChoices.shortLabel: Freeze all updates until next year
presentationChoices.fullDescription: Delay every change regardless of the vulnerability.
presentationChoices.feedback: A blanket freeze can leave serious exposure open long after the deadline pressure ends.

twist.headline: New information
twist.revealText: The vendor reports exploitation of the vulnerable feature. A temporary mitigation is available, but disables one optional integration.
twist.reconsiderQuestion: Does your original plan still work?

completion.takeaway: Change decisions must protect both security and the opportunity.
completion.action: Within 30 days, rehearse a deadline change-control decision with threat evidence, rollback, secure fallback, and a named authority.
